subject: Art & Design
title: Street Photography: Capturing Everyday Life
description: A 60-second lesson on Street Photography: Capturing Everyday Life.

hook.text: A woman's hat blows off in the wind. A stranger reaches to catch it. One frame captures the entire moment.

buildup.text: Street photography documents unposed human moments in public spaces. It's raw, unscripted, real.

discovery.text: The genre requires invisibility: blend in, anticipate, and capture without disrupting the scene.

twist.text: Legal debates rage: in most countries, photographing in public is legal. Ethics is a separate question.

climax.text: Vivian Maier shot 100,000+ street photos. They were only discovered after she died. Now she's legendary.

punchline.text: The best street photo is the one nobody posed for.

quiz.question: What makes street photography unique as a genre?
options: It captures unposed, spontaneous human moments in public
It requires the most expensive equipment
It can only be shot in cities

details.summary: Street photography documents candid moments in public spaces — the spontaneous interactions, expressions, and absurdities of everyday life. It requires both technical skill and social courage, capturing unposed, unrehearsed human behavior that reveals the poetry of ordinary existence.
details.whyItMatters: Street photography preserves moments that would otherwise disappear. It finds beauty and meaning in the mundane, creating visual records of how people actually live rather than how they pose. It's photography as social observation.
takeaways: Street photography captures candid moments in public spaces
It reveals the poetry and absurdity of everyday human life
The genre requires both technical skill and social courage

faq.question: Is street photography legal?
faq.answer: In most countries, photographing people in public spaces is legal without consent for non-commercial artistic use. Laws vary — France requires consent for identifiable faces in some contexts, while the US broadly protects public photography. Ethical considerations often matter more than legal ones.

faq.question: What camera settings work best for street photography?
faq.answer: Aperture priority around f/8 for sufficient depth of field, auto ISO with a minimum shutter speed of 1/250s to freeze motion, and zone focusing (pre-focusing at a set distance) for fast response. Small cameras and prime lenses (35mm or 50mm) are traditional street photography tools.
